docs.title: Zeta
docs.text:
Zeta is a Kubernetes build portal for developers without user kubeconfigs. Developers submit builds from their workstation with the zeta CLI. The portal runs inside the cluster, creates Kubernetes Jobs with its own ServiceAccount, and streams logs, metrics, artifacts, and optional bidirectional workspace sync back to the CLI.

The web UI is a monitoring dashboard, not a build form.

  • :material-server-network:{ .lg .middle } Operate the platform

    Install the portal with Helm, configure OIDC and storage, and run upgrades.

    :octicons-arrow-right-24: Platform overview

  • :material-laptop:{ .lg .middle } Build with Zeta

    Install the CLI with curl | sh or PowerShell, then build without a kubeconfig.

    :octicons-arrow-right-24: Developer overview

  • :material-console:{ .lg .middle } Use the CLI

    Local or Git builds, live logs, artifacts, volumes, and environments.

    :octicons-arrow-right-24: CLI guide

  • :material-sitemap:{ .lg .middle } Understand the architecture

    Control plane, execution plane, Jobs, PVCs, and the sync hub.

    :octicons-arrow-right-24: Architecture

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
Platform teamDeveloper 
helm upgrade --install zeta oci://ghcr.io/slimaineb/charts/zeta \
  --version 0.1.0 \
  --namespace zeta-poc --create-namespace \
  --set ingress.host=zeta.local

See Install the platform.

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SlimaineB/zeta/main/scripts/install-cli.sh | sh
zeta login --server http://zeta.local --email dev@example.com --password dev
cd my-project
zeta build

On Windows:

irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SlimaineB/zeta/main/scripts/install-cli.ps1 | iex

See Install the CLI.

docs.title: What Zeta gives you
docs.text:
• Compute on demand. One of the main goals of Zeta is to avoid keeping a powerful workstation or build server running all the time. Builds run in short-lived Kubernetes Jobs, so CPU and memory are used only while a build is running. Persistent environments scale to zero when idle.
  • Zero Kubernetes onboarding. No kubeconfig, no namespace access, no kubectl knowledge required.
  • Reproducible environments. Every build uses a pinned image and profile, so local machine differences do not affect the result.
  • Isolation. Builds run as non-root Jobs under restricted Pod Security, without service account tokens.
  • Fast feedback. Logs stream live, caches persist between builds, and artifacts are downloaded automatically.
  • Flexible source input. Use the local working tree by default, or a pushed Git commit when you need an auditable revision.
  • Interactive debugging. --sync mirrors your local code into the build pod and brings produced files back.
  • Persistent dev environments. zeta activate opens a shell and zeta code opens VS Code in the browser, both backed by the same pod that stays available between commands, backed by a persistent volume.
  • Extensible. A new language is a YAML profile plus an image, not a control plane change.

docs.text:
flowchart LR
  subgraph workstation["Developer workstation"]
    CLI["zeta CLI"]
  end

  subgraph cluster["Kubernetes cluster"]
    Portal["Zeta portal"]
    API["Kubernetes API"]
    Job["Build Job"]
    Env["Environment<br/>replicas 0 or 1"]
    Cache[("cache PVC")]
    Artifacts[("artifacts PVC")]

  CLI -->|"HTTP + session cookie"| Portal
  Portal -->|"ServiceAccount + RBAC"| API
  API --> Job
  API --> Env
  Job --> Cache
  Job --> Artifacts
  Portal -->|"logs, metrics, artifacts"| CLI

The build Job is ephemeral: it is created when you run zeta build and removed after completion. Only the cache and artifacts PVCs remain.

For persistent environments, the workload is not an ephemeral Job:

zeta CLI  <--- WebSocket --->  portal sync hub  <--- WebSocket --->  syncd
       |                                                                |
       |  interactive shell (exec)                                      v
       `------------------------------------------------------>  /workspace (PVC)

docs.title: What Zeta is not
docs.text:
• It is not a full CI/CD system with SCM webhooks, pipelines, approvals, and deployment stages.
  • It does not provide full per-group RBAC or strong multi-tenant isolation yet; builds and environments are owner-scoped with an admin override.
  • It does not build or push OCI images; it produces build artifacts on a PVC.
  • It is not a remote cache or a distributed build system for very large monorepos.

docs.title: Project status
docs.text:
Zeta is under active development and is validated on a single-node k3s cluster (WSL2). The following are implemented and tested:

  • local and Git builds, C++/Python/Go profiles, persistent caches;
  • artifacts, metrics, web dashboard, and HTTP API;
  • persistent environments with shell, file sync, and idle scale-down;
  • volume quotas, resize, and deletion;
  • dev and OIDC authentication.

Known limitations are documented in Security and Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Developer overview
docs.text:
Zeta lets you build and debug projects in the cluster without a kubeconfig. You use a single binary, zeta, from Windows, macOS, or Linux. Builds always run in Linux pods.

The platform team installs the portal and the build images. See Platform overview. You only need the CLI and a login.

docs.title: Install the CLI
docs.text:
Linux and macOS:

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SlimaineB/zeta/main/scripts/install-cli.sh | sh

Windows PowerShell:

irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SlimaineB/zeta/main/scripts/install-cli.ps1 | iex

The installers download the matching binary from the latest GitHub Release, verify checksums.txt, and put zeta on your PATH. See Install the CLI for pinned versions and manual downloads.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  subgraph local["Your workstation"]
    Dev["Project files"]
    CLI["zeta CLI<br/>Windows, macOS, Linux"]
  end

  subgraph cluster["Kubernetes cluster"]
    Portal["Zeta portal"]
    Job["Linux build pod"]
    Env["Persistent environment"]
  end

  Dev --> CLI
  CLI -->|"context + session cookie"| Portal
  Portal -->|"creates"| Job
  Portal -->|"creates"| Env
  Job -->|"logs, artifacts, sync"| CLI
  Env -->|"shell + sync"| CLI
  • The CLI packages the local context and uploads it; no Git remote is required.
  • The portal creates a Job with the selected profile image.
  • Logs stream live; artifacts come back as an archive.
  • zeta build --sync mirrors your local directory into the pod and back.
  • Persistent environments stay available between commands and scale to zero when idle.

docs.title: Install the CLI
docs.text: The zeta CLI is a single static binary. You do not need Go, Docker, or kubectl to use it.

docs.title: Linux and macOS
docs.text:
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SlimaineB/zeta/main/scripts/install-cli.sh | sh

The installer:

  1. detects Linux or macOS and amd64 or arm64;
  2. downloads zeta-<os>-<arch> from the latest GitHub Release;
  3. verifies it against checksums.txt;
  4. installs it to ~/.local/bin/zeta.

Choose another directory or pin a version:

ZETA_BIN_DIR="$HOME/bin" \
  curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SlimaineB/zeta/main/scripts/install-cli.sh | sh

ZETA_VERSION=0.1.0 \
  curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SlimaineB/zeta/main/scripts/install-cli.sh | sh

If ~/.local/bin is not on your PATH, the installer prints the line to add to your shell profile.

docs.title: Windows
docs.text:
In PowerShell:

irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SlimaineB/zeta/main/scripts/install-cli.ps1 | iex

The script installs zeta.exe to %LOCALAPPDATA%\zeta\bin and adds that directory to your user PATH. Open a new terminal afterward.

Pinned version or custom directory:

$env:ZETA_VERSION = "0.1.0"
$env:ZETA_BIN_DIR = "$HOME\bin"
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SlimaineB/zeta/main/scripts/install-cli.ps1 | iex

The CLI works on Windows, but builds run in Linux pods. File sync, shells, and artifact downloads behave the same as on Linux.

docs.title: Manual download
docs.text:
Every release contains:

Asset Platform zeta-linux-amd64 Linux x86-64 zeta-linux-arm64 Linux ARM64 zeta-darwin-amd64 macOS Intel zeta-darwin-arm64 macOS Apple silicon zeta-windows-amd64.exe Windows x86-64 zeta-windows-arm64.exe Windows ARM64 checksums.txt SHA-256 checksums

Download from https://github.com/SlimaineB/zeta/releases. On Linux or macOS:

VERSION=v0.1.0
curl -fLO "https://github.com/SlimaineB/zeta/releases/download/${VERSION}/zeta-linux-amd64"
curl -fLO "https://github.com/SlimaineB/zeta/releases/download/${VERSION}/checksums.txt"
sha256sum --check --ignore-missing checksums.txt
install -m 0755 zeta-linux-amd64 ~/.local/bin/zeta

docs.title: Build from source
docs.text:
cd cli
make build
./bin/zeta help

Or install it with the repository helper:

make install-user

The source build requires Go 1.26 or newer. This is only needed for development; users should prefer the release binaries.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
zeta help

zeta help lists the commands. If the shell cannot find the binary, check your PATH.

docs.title: Log in
docs.text:
Development authentication:

zeta login --server http://zeta.local --email dev@example.com --password dev

The session is stored in ~/.config/zeta/config.json with mode 0600. The server can also be set with ZETA_SERVER.

OIDC browser login is not integrated into the CLI yet. Copy the zeta_session cookie from the browser and run:

zeta login --server https://zeta.example.com --cookie '<cookie_value>'

docs.title: Adding a build profile
docs.text:
1. Create an image under platform/images/<name>/.
  2. Add a build target and import step in platform/scripts/build-images.sh.
  3. Add a profile to portal/internal/builds/defaults.yaml.
  4. Document the profile in docs/user-guide/profiles.md.
  5. Test with zeta profiles and a small build.
  6. Run go test ./... and go vet ./....

A profile is just YAML: name, language, image, commands, artifact path, cache, resources, env, and metrics.

docs.title: Code style
docs.text:
• Run gofmt on Go files.
  • Keep packages focused; the portal is split into auth, builds, config, domain, httpapi, kube, sync, and ui.
  • Prefer small, testable functions.
  • Add tests for behavior changes, especially around resource creation and API handlers.
  • Do not log secrets.
  • Keep user-facing messages consistent.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
The docs are split into docs/platform/ (Helm, operations) and docs/developer/ (CLI, first build). Keep the two audiences separate and make sure cross-links resolve.

The docs use MkDocs Material:

python3 -m venv .venv-docs
. .venv-docs/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements-docs.txt
mkdocs serve

Build with strict links:

mkdocs build --strict

The GitHub Actions workflow publishes to gh-pages on pushes to main.

docs.title: Pull request checklist
docs.text:
• go test ./... passes in portal and cli.
  • go vet ./... passes in portal and cli.
  • mkdocs build --strict passes if docs changed.
  • New behavior is documented.
  • No secrets, kubeconfigs, or tokens are committed.
  • The change is tested on a local k3s cluster when it touches Kubernetes resources.
  • Commits have a clear, focused message.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Zeta has two installation paths:

  • Platform team: install the portal, RBAC, and PVCs with Helm. See Install the platform.
  • Developers: install the zeta CLI with curl | sh or PowerShell. See Install the CLI.

For a local k3s cluster without a registry, use the source installer:

./scripts/install.sh

See Platform overview for the local build path, and First build after installation.

docs.title: First build
docs.text: This guide assumes the portal is already installed. If not, follow Install the platform and Install the CLI.

docs.title: 1. Log in
docs.text:
zeta login --server http://zeta.local --email dev@example.com --password dev

The session is stored in ~/.config/zeta/config.json with mode 0600.

docs.title: 2. Check profiles
docs.text:
zeta profiles

NAME    LANGUAGE  DEFAULT REPO                     DESCRIPTION
cpp     cpp       git://git-server/cpp.git         C++ CMake/Ninja with persistent ccache
go      go        git://git-server/go.git          Go modules with persistent GOCACHE/GOMODCACHE
python  python    git://git-server/python-uv.git   Python 3.12 + uv with persistent uv cache

docs.title: 3. Run a local build
docs.text:
From a project directory:

cd my-project
zeta build

The CLI detects the profile from the files present:

Detected file Profile CMakeLists.txt cpp go.mod go pyproject.toml, setup.py, requirements.txt python

It packages the context as a tar.gz, uploads it, streams logs, waits for completion, and extracts artifacts into artifacts/<id>.

Example output:

context: /home/user/my-project (27 KB)
build zeta-cpp-xxxxxxxxxxxx (cpp) context /home/user/my-project
--- logs ---
[ live build logs ]
build succeeded in 5.0 s
cache: 7 hits / 1 miss (88%) · 43 KB
artifacts: /home/user/my-project/artifacts/zeta-cpp-xxxxxxxxxxxx

docs.title: 4. Force a profile or adjust the build
docs.text:
# Force the profile
zeta build --profile go

# Exclude files from the context
zeta build --exclude .cache --exclude docs

# Do not follow logs
zeta build --follow=false

# Do not download artifacts
zeta build --artifacts=false

# Choose the output directory
zeta build --artifacts-dir ./out

# Timeout (30m by default)
zeta build --timeout 10m

docs.title: 5. Build from Git
docs.text:
Git mode builds a commit that is already pushed and reachable from the cluster:

zeta build --git --profile go \
  --repo git://git-server/go.git \
  --commit main

With the example Git server, the in-cluster URL is git://git-server/<repo>.git.

docs.title: 6. Interactive sync
docs.text:
To edit locally during the build and recover files produced inside the pod:

zeta build --sync

The build waits for the /workspace/.zeta-ready marker, syncs the initial context, then exchanges changes in both directions. --sync is incompatible with Git mode.

docs.title: 7. Persistent environment
docs.text:
An environment is a pod that stays available between commands, backed by a persistent volume and a bidirectional mirror of your local directory.

cd my-project
zeta init                 # create the volume, secret, and stopped deployment
zeta activate             # start the pod, open a shell, and sync files
zeta ls                   # list environments
zeta deactivate           # scale the pod to zero, keep the volume
zeta rm                   # delete everything, including the volume

A zeta.yaml file at the project root avoids repeating options:

name: my-project
profile: go
image: zeta/go:0.1
size: 5Gi
env:
  GOFLAGS: -mod=mod

See Persistent environments and zeta.yaml reference.

docs.title: Deployment and operations
docs.text: This page covers day-two operations: upgrades, logs, cleanup, releases, and documentation publishing.

docs.title: Update the platform with Helm
docs.text:
The recommended upgrade path is the published chart:

helm upgrade --install zeta oci://ghcr.io/slimaineb/charts/zeta \
  --version 0.2.0 \
  --namespace zeta-poc \
  --reuse-values

Review the new defaults before upgrading:

helm show values oci://ghcr.io/slimaineb/charts/zeta --version 0.2.0

--reuse-values keeps your previous overrides. The chart updates the portal, RBAC, and optional Git server; shared PVCs are preserved. The portal image and helper images (context init, syncd, Git server) use the chart version by default.

See the Helm chart reference for values and examples.

docs.title: Deploy from source
docs.text:
On a local k3s cluster, build the images and install the local chart:

./scripts/install.sh

Or use the Make target:

make install-smart

The raw manifest path remains available for development:

cd portal
make test
make deploy

make deploy compiles the portal, builds zeta/portal:0.1, imports it into k3s, applies platform/manifests/portal.yaml, and waits for the rollout. From the repository root, make install-platform rebuilds the images and reapplies the raw manifests.

docs.title: Build and import images
docs.text:
cd platform
make images

This builds the language images and the Git server image, then imports them into k3s containerd. To re-import a single image:

docker save zeta/go:0.1 | sudo -n k3s ctr images import -

docs.title: Install or update the CLI
docs.text:
Users should install the release binary:

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SlimaineB/zeta/main/scripts/install-cli.sh | sh

On Windows:

irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SlimaineB/zeta/main/scripts/install-cli.ps1 | iex

For a source build:

make install-user

Or manually:

cd cli
make build
sudo install -m 0755 bin/zeta /usr/local/bin/zeta

See Install the CLI.

docs.title: Release pipeline
docs.text:
The release workflow runs on v* tags. For v0.1.0 it publishes:

  • images ghcr.io/<owner>/zeta/{portal,cpp,go,python-uv,git-server}:0.1.0 and :latest;
  • CLI assets zeta-{linux,darwin,windows}-{amd64,arm64};
  • the Helm chart at oci://ghcr.io/<owner>/charts/zeta:0.1.0;
  • a GitHub Release with the binaries, chart, and checksums.txt.

The chart package is patched with the release registry, so a plain helm install uses the published images. The workflow also attempts to make the GHCR packages public. If a package stays private, follow the private registry steps.

docs.title: Status
docs.text:
make status
helm status zeta -n zeta-poc

Useful checks:

kubectl --context local -n zeta-poc get deploy,svc,ingress,pods,pvc
kubectl --context local -n zeta-poc get jobs
kubectl --context local -n zeta-poc get events --sort-by=.lastTimestamp

docs.title: Logs
docs.text:
kubectl --context local -n zeta-poc logs deploy/zeta-portal -f

Or:

cd portal
make logs

Environment sync logs:

kubectl --context local -n zeta-poc logs deploy/zeta-env-<id> -c syncd

docs.title: Restart k3s under WSL
docs.text:
sudo -n bash -c 'nohup k3s server >/tmp/k3s-server.log 2>&1 &'
kubectl --context local get nodes

docs.title: Clean up builds
docs.text:
Jobs have a 1-hour TTL. Manual deletion:

kubectl --context local -n zeta-poc delete job \
  -l zeta.io/managed-by=portal

docs.title: Reset the cache
docs.text:
Shared cache

This removes ccache, uv, and Go caches for every build using the shared PVC.

zeta volumes --role cache
kubectl --context local -n zeta-poc delete job \
  -l zeta.io/managed-by=portal --ignore-not-found
kubectl --context local -n zeta-poc delete pvc zeta-poc-cache

The PVC is recreated on the next build. Profiles with a dedicated cachePVC keep their own volume.

docs.title: Reset artifacts
docs.text:
zeta volumes --role artifacts
kubectl --context local -n zeta-poc delete pvc zeta-poc-artifacts

The shared PVC is recreated on the next build.

docs.title: Reset an environment
docs.text:
zeta deactivate --name dev      # keep the workspace
zeta rm dev                     # delete the workspace and secret

If rm reports that the volume is still terminating, wait for the finalizer and retry.

docs.title: Uninstall
docs.text:
helm uninstall zeta -n zeta-poc

The shared PVCs have helm.sh/resource-policy: keep, so Helm leaves the cache, artifacts, and environment workspaces in place. To remove everything:

kubectl delete namespace zeta-poc

For a raw installation:

make uninstall-platform

This deletes the zeta-poc namespace: portal, Git server, Jobs, PVCs, and environment workspaces. Imported images remain in containerd.

docs.title: GitHub Pages
docs.text:
The workflow .github/workflows/docs.yml runs on every push to main that changes docs/, mkdocs.yml, or requirements-docs.txt. It installs requirements-docs.txt and runs:

mkdocs gh-deploy --force

This publishes to the gh-pages branch. The repository Pages source is:

  • branch gh-pages;
  • folder / (root).

The site is available at https://slimaineb.github.io/zeta/.

If the URL returns a GitHub Pages 404:

  1. open Settings → Pages;
  2. set Source to Deploy from a branch;
  3. choose gh-pages and / (root);
  4. save, then wait for the Pages build to finish.

You can also trigger the docs workflow manually from the Actions tab.

docs.title: Upgrade checklist
docs.text:
1. Review the release notes and helm show values.
  2. Back up any data you cannot recreate.
  3. helm upgrade --install zeta ... --reuse-values.
  4. Update the CLI with the install script.
  5. zeta login.
  6. Run a smoke build and zeta ls.

docs.title: Backup notes
docs.text:
• PVC data (caches, artifacts, environment workspaces) is not backed up by the portal.
  • Back up environment workspaces from inside the pod, or snapshot the underlying storage.
  • Helm configuration lives in your values file or --set overrides. Raw configuration lives in platform/manifests/portal.yaml and the profiles YAML.

docs.title: Security
docs.text: This page describes Zeta's security model, its guarantees, and its current limitations.

docs.title: Security model
docs.text:
• Developers never receive a kubeconfig.
  • The portal uses a namespace-scoped ServiceAccount.
  • Jobs and environments run as non-root 1000:1000 with no service account token.
  • Pod Security Admission restricted, seccomp RuntimeDefault, all capabilities dropped.
  • The portal root filesystem is read-only.
  • Build context archives are validated against path traversal, out-of-context links, and special files.
  • Sync paths are validated and dangerous symlinks are rejected.

docs.title: Authentication and sessions
docs.text:
The portal supports two modes:

  • Development mode (--oidc-dev): built-in users and passwords, intended for local use only.
  • OIDC: authorization code flow with PKCE, nonce verification, the configured issuer, client ID, secret, scopes, and callback URL.

The short-lived login state is stored in a signed zeta_oidc cookie, not in process memory, so login works with multiple portal replicas. Sessions are signed with an HMAC key (--oidc-session-key) and stored in the zeta_session cookie. If no key is provided, a random key is generated at startup; all sessions are invalidated on restart.

OIDC claims are configurable with --oidc-username-claim, --oidc-email-claim, and --oidc-groups-claim. Groups and profile data are merged from the userinfo endpoint when missing from the ID token. --oidc-allowed-groups and --oidc-allowed-users optionally restrict who can sign in; when both are set, a user must match both allowlists.

In production:

  • set a fixed, random session key of at least 32 characters;
  • set --secure-cookie behind HTTPS;
  • keep the session TTL short enough for your policy (default 12h);
  • configure the OIDC provider to allow exactly the callback URL;
  • use an allowlist when the provider can authenticate users outside your team.

docs.title: Transport and browser protections
docs.text:
• Browser WebSocket endpoints (/api/envs/{id}/exec and /api/sync/{id}/client) require an Origin header matching the portal host.
  • The sync agent authenticates with Authorization: Bearer <token>. The older ?token= query parameter is still accepted for backward compatibility but is no longer used by newly created environments or build Jobs.
  • State-changing API requests reject cross-site Sec-Fetch-Site, Origin, or Referer values. Non-browser clients that send none of these headers, such as the CLI, are still accepted.
  • The session cookie is signed but not encrypted. It contains identity and group data, not credentials. Logout clears the local cookie; the portal does not implement IdP-initiated or RP-initiated revocation yet.

docs.title: Authorization
docs.text:
The portal's ServiceAccount is namespace-scoped. It can create and inspect Jobs, Pods, Pod logs, Deployments, Secrets, and PVCs in zeta-poc.

Environments and builds are owner-scoped. The portal records the authenticated user's email (or username when the provider omits email) as the owner when creating an environment or build. Lifecycle operations, exec, sync, logs, metrics, and artifact downloads require the owner or membership in the admin / admins group. Listing builds and environments remains available to every authenticated user. Resources created before owner tracking, or with an empty owner, remain accessible to any authenticated user for backward compatibility.

There is still no full per-group RBAC, and volumes remain shared across the namespace. The groups claim is collected and can be used in --oidc-allowed-groups, but it is not used for arbitrary group-to-resource policy.

docs.title: Pod security
docs.text:
Build Jobs and environment pods use:

  • runAsNonRoot: true, runAsUser: 1000, runAsGroup: 1000;
  • automountServiceAccountToken: false;
  • seccompProfile: RuntimeDefault;
  • all Linux capabilities dropped;
  • no privileged mode, no host namespaces, no host paths.

The portal itself runs as non-root 65532:65532 with a read-only root filesystem.

docs.title: Browser IDE
docs.text:
The code-server sidecar is part of the environment pod and shares /workspace. It binds to 127.0.0.1:8080; no Service or Ingress exposes it. The browser reaches it only through /api/envs/<id>/ide/ on the portal:

  • the portal requires a valid session and checks environment ownership;
  • the portal opens a Kubernetes port-forward (pods/portforward) to the pod;
  • HTTP and WebSocket traffic is reverse-proxied, including the VS Code extension-host socket;
  • code-server authentication is disabled because the portal is the authentication boundary;
  • the port-forward is closed when the environment is deactivated, deleted, or reaped;
  • an open IDE WebSocket counts as activity and prevents idle scale-down.

The portal service account therefore needs get and create on pods/portforward in the environment namespace.

docs.title: Context validation
docs.text:
The portal validates uploaded archives:

  • no absolute paths;
  • no .. traversal;
  • no links escaping the context;
  • no special files (devices, sockets, etc.);
  • upload limited to 512 MiB (2 GiB uncompressed).

Git mode validates the repository URL scheme and rejects shell metacharacters and .. in references.

docs.title: Sync validation
docs.text: The sync client and server validate paths and reject dangerous symlinks. Sync is scoped to the workspace and the configured exclusions.

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text:
• Build secrets are injected with envFromSecrets and marked optional: true.
  • The example zeta-build-secrets Secret holds GIT_TOKEN, GIT_USERNAME, and Go proxy settings.
  • Environment sync tokens are stored in zeta-env-<id>-sync and mounted only into the syncd container.
  • The portal never logs secret values.

Use Kubernetes Secrets, not literals in profiles, for credentials.

docs.title: Limits and known gaps
docs.text:
• No full per-group RBAC or strong multi-tenant isolation; volumes remain shared.
  • No IdP logout/revocation; sessions remain valid until expiry after local logout.
  • The session cookie is signed but not encrypted.
  • No private SSH repository support; use HTTPS tokens.
  • Artifacts are stored per language path, not per build.
  • No S3/MinIO backend; PVCs use local-path on the reference single-node cluster.
  • No automatic volume garbage collection.
  • Volume expansion requires a StorageClass with allowVolumeExpansion: true.
  • Jobs and artifacts expire after one hour by default.
  • No .dockerignore; use --exclude and default context exclusions.

docs.title: Hardening checklist
docs.text:
• Replace dev auth with OIDC.
  • Set a fixed --oidc-session-key.
  • Enable --secure-cookie and serve the portal over HTTPS.
  • Use an EBS-backed StorageClass with encryption.
  • Restrict network access to the ingress.
  • Review the portal RBAC and namespace scope.
  • Create build secrets with least privilege.
  • Monitor portal and Job logs.
  • Keep images pinned and rebuilt on security updates.
  • Back up persistent environment workspaces.

docs.title: Reporting a vulnerability
docs.text: Do not open a public issue for a security problem. Contact the repository owner privately and include a description, reproduction steps, and impact.

docs.title: Quick diagnostics
docs.text:
make doctor
kubectl --context local get nodes
kubectl --context local -n zeta-poc get deploy,svc,ingress,pods,pvc,jobs
kubectl --context local -n zeta-poc logs deploy/zeta-portal --tail=100

docs.title: The connection to the server 127.0.0.1:6443 was refused
docs.text:
k3s is not running. Restart it:

sudo -n bash -c 'nohup k3s server >/tmp/k3s-server.log 2>&1 &'
kubectl --context local get nodes

docs.title: zeta: session missing; run zeta login
docs.text:
The CLI has no local session. Run:

zeta login --server http://zeta.local --email dev@example.com --password dev

docs.title: not authenticated or session expired
docs.text: The cookie is invalid or expired. Run zeta login again. If the portal restarted without a fixed --oidc-session-key, all sessions were invalidated.

docs.title: OIDC sign-in fails or redirects back to login
docs.text:
Check that:

  • the provider callback URL is exactly https://<host>/oidc/callback;
  • --oidc-issuer matches the issuer returned by discovery;
  • --oidc-discovery-url is reachable from the portal if you use a split-horizon discovery endpoint;
  • the user matches --oidc-allowed-groups and --oidc-allowed-users when those allowlists are configured;
  • all replicas use the same --oidc-session-key; the short-lived zeta_oidc flow cookie is signed with it.

If the provider returns groups only through userinfo, make sure the groups scope is requested or set --oidc-groups-claim to the claim your provider uses.

docs.title: Ingress 404
docs.text:
The Host header does not match zeta.local. Check the hosts entry or use a port-forward:

kubectl --context local -n zeta-poc port-forward \
  --address 0.0.0.0 svc/zeta-portal 8080:80

docs.title: Port-forward not reachable from Windows
docs.text:
Use --address 0.0.0.0:

kubectl --context local -n zeta-poc port-forward \
  --address 0.0.0.0 svc/zeta-portal 8080:80

docs.title: invalid repository URL
docs.text: Use git://, http://, https://, or ssh://. file:// URLs and local paths are rejected.

docs.title: invalid Git reference
docs.text: The commit contains forbidden characters (.., spaces, ;, $, etc.). Use a SHA, tag, or simple branch name.

docs.title: remote HEAD refers to nonexistent ref
docs.text:
The bare repository points at a missing branch. Fix it:

kubectl --context local -n zeta-poc exec deploy/git-server -- \
  sh -c 'git --git-dir=/srv/git/cpp.git symbolic-ref HEAD refs/heads/main'

docs.title: dubious ownership in a Job
docs.text: The Job configures safe.directory /workspace. If a custom profile clones elsewhere, add the same Git configuration.

docs.title: ImagePullBackOff / ErrImageNeverPull
docs.text:
The image is not present in k3s containerd. Re-import it:

docker save zeta/go:0.1 | sudo -n k3s ctr images import -

Or rebuild all images:

cd platform
make images

docs.title: Build stuck in Pending
docs.text:
Check PVCs and the StorageClass:

kubectl --context local -n zeta-poc get pvc
kubectl --context local get storageclass
kubectl --context local -n zeta-poc describe pod <pod>

The reference k3s setup uses local-path.

docs.title: PodInitializing in logs
docs.text:
Context extraction (tar or Git clone) is still running. Wait or inspect the init container logs:

kubectl --context local -n zeta-poc logs <pod> -c context

docs.title: Context too large (413)
docs.text:
The upload is limited to 512 MiB. Exclude large directories:

zeta build --exclude node_modules --exclude data

docs.title: Builds disappear after one hour
docs.text: This is the Job TTL (TTLSecondsAfterFinished: 3600). Change it in portal/internal/kube/repository.go and redeploy for longer retention.

docs.title: Artifact download fails with unexpected EOF
docs.text:
Artifacts are streamed as gzip+base64 through pod logs to avoid binary log corruption. Check the portal logs and the Job status:

kubectl --context local -n zeta-poc logs deploy/zeta-portal --tail=100
zeta status <id>

docs.title: activate: environment <id> not found
docs.text: zeta activate only starts an existing environment. Create it first with zeta init, then run zeta activate again.

docs.title: zeta activate hangs
docs.text:
Check the pod and the sync sidecar:

kubectl --context local -n zeta-poc get pods
kubectl --context local -n zeta-poc logs deploy/zeta-env-<id> -c syncd
kubectl --context local -n zeta-poc logs deploy/zeta-env-<id> -c env

Common causes: missing image, PVC not bound, or the portal cannot reach the Deployment.

docs.title: Shell exits immediately
docs.text: The profile image must contain a shell (sh or bash). Check the env container logs and the image entrypoint.

docs.title: Files do not come back locally
docs.text:
• build/ and dist/ are synced back, but .git, .venv, caches, and node_modules are excluded.
  • Check exclude in zeta.yaml and --exclude.
  • Confirm the sync session is still connected.

docs.title: zeta code says the IDE is not ready
docs.text:
The first zeta code call adds the ide sidecar to an existing environment and triggers a rollout. Wait for the new pod, then retry:

kubectl --context local -n zeta-poc get pods -l zeta.io/env=<id>
kubectl --context local -n zeta-poc logs deploy/zeta-env-<id> -c ide

If the pod stays 2/3, check that codercom/code-server:4.143.1 is present on the node (or pullable) and that the portal Role includes pods/portforward. The sidecar binds to 127.0.0.1:8080, so a normal HTTP probe from kubelet cannot reach it; the portal waits for the container and opens a port-forward instead.

docs.title: Environment stops by itself
docs.text: This is the idle reaper. Default --env-idle-timeout is 15m; 0 disables it. Run zeta activate again to resume with the same volume.

docs.title: rm returns 504
docs.text:
The portal restarted during the request or the PVC is still terminating. Retry:

zeta rm <id>

If the PVC is stuck:

kubectl --context local -n zeta-poc get pvc zeta-env-<id>
kubectl --context local -n zeta-poc describe pvc zeta-env-<id>

docs.title: Namespace stuck in Terminating
docs.text:
Check for remaining namespaced resources and finalizers:

kubectl --context local get ns <name> -o yaml
kubectl --context local -n <name> get all,pvc,secret,sa,role,rolebinding

Delete remaining workloads and PVCs, then wait for the namespace controller. As a last resort, clear the namespace finalizer through the finalize subresource.

docs.title: Resize fails
docs.text:
• The volume is in use by a build.
  • The StorageClass does not support expansion. local-path does not; use an EBS-backed class with allowVolumeExpansion: true.

docs.title: Quota exceeded
docs.text: Check zeta volumes and raise --volume-quota / --volume-max, or delete an unused volume.

docs.title: Logs and debugging
docs.text:
# Portal
kubectl --context local -n zeta-poc logs deploy/zeta-portal -f

# Build pod
kubectl --context local -n zeta-poc get pods
kubectl --context local -n zeta-poc describe pod <pod>
kubectl --context local -n zeta-poc logs <pod> -c context
kubectl --context local -n zeta-poc logs <pod> -c build

# Environment
kubectl --context local -n zeta-poc logs deploy/zeta-env-<id> -c env
kubectl --context local -n zeta-poc logs deploy/zeta-env-<id> -c syncd

# Events
kubectl --context local -n zeta-poc get events --sort-by=.lastTimestamp

docs.title: Platform overview
docs.text:
This section is for the team that operates the Kubernetes cluster. Developers only need the CLI; they do not need a kubeconfig, a namespace, or kubectl.

Zeta runs as a normal Kubernetes Deployment. The portal owns the build namespace, creates short-lived Jobs, and exposes a small HTTP API and dashboard. The platform team installs and upgrades it with Helm.

docs.title: What you deploy
docs.text:
Component Managed by Purpose Portal Deployment Helm API, authentication, dashboard, Job creation Service and Ingress Helm HTTPS entry point RBAC Helm Namespace-scoped access to Jobs, Pods, logs, and PVCs Shared PVCs Helm Cache, artifacts, and uploaded contexts Build images Release pipeline C++, Go, Python/uv, Git server, portal/syncd Optional Git server Helm Example repositories for Git-mode builds

The chart keeps the resource names stable: the portal is zeta-portal, the Git server Service is git-server, and the PVCs are zeta-poc-artifacts, zeta-poc-cache, and zeta-poc-contexts. Profiles and the CLI rely on these names.

docs.title: Compute on demand
docs.text:
One of the main goals of Zeta is to avoid keeping a powerful build workstation or CI server running all the time. A small shared cluster is enough:

  • a build runs in an ephemeral Job and releases its CPU and memory when it finishes;
  • caches and artifacts stay on PVCs, not on always-on build machines;
  • persistent environments scale to zero when no shell or sync client is attached, then resume from the same volume.
flowchart TB
  subgraph workstation["Developer workstation"]
    CLI["zeta CLI"]
  end

  subgraph cluster["Kubernetes cluster"]
    Ingress["Ingress"] --> Portal["Portal Deployment"]
    Portal --> API["Kubernetes API"]
    API --> Jobs["Build Jobs<br/>ephemeral"]
    API --> Envs["Environment Deployments<br/>0 or 1 replica"]
    Jobs --> Cache[("cache PVC")]
    Jobs --> Artifacts[("artifacts PVC")]
    Portal --> Contexts[("contexts PVC")]
    API --> Git["optional Git server"]
  end

  CLI -->|"HTTP + session cookie"| Ingress
  Jobs -->|"logs, artifacts, sync"| Portal

Only the portal, the optional Git server, and the PVCs remain after a build.

docs.title: Install the platform
docs.text:
The published chart already points at the GHCR images:

helm upgrade --install zeta oci://ghcr.io/slimaineb/charts/zeta \
  --version 0.1.0 \
  --namespace zeta-poc --create-namespace \
  --set ingress.host=zeta.local

If your cluster does not use Traefik or local-path storage:

helm upgrade --install zeta oci://ghcr.io/slimaineb/charts/zeta \
  --version 0.1.0 \
  --namespace zeta-poc --create-namespace \
  --set ingress.className=nginx \
  --set ingress.host=zeta.example.com \
  --set portal.storageClass=gp3

Then point zeta.local (or your host) at the ingress address:

kubectl -n zeta-poc get ingress zeta-portal

The default development login is dev@example.com / dev. For production, configure OIDC and a fixed session key. See the Helm chart reference.

docs.title: Install from source
docs.text:
For local development or a k3s cluster without a registry, the smart installer builds the images, imports them into k3s, and runs the same Helm chart:

./scripts/install.sh

Useful variants:

./scripts/install.sh --with-git-server
./scripts/install.sh --adopt        # migrate an existing raw install
./scripts/install.sh --dry-run      # print the Helm command only

The installer is idempotent. make install-smart is the same command.

docs.title: Helm chart reference
docs.text:
The chart lives in charts/zeta and is published as an OCI artifact:

helm show values oci://ghcr.io/slimaineb/charts/zeta --version 0.1.0

docs.title: Images
docs.text:
Value Default Description image.registry ghcr.io/slimaineb in the published chart Registry prefix for all Zeta images image.repository zeta/portal Portal repository image.tag chart appVersion Portal tag; also used for syncd, init, and Git server images image.pullPolicy IfNotPresent Pull policy image.pullSecrets [] Pull secrets for the portal and Git server

The portal receives -image-registry and -image-tag, so profile images and helper images (context init, syncd, Git server) are rewritten consistently. For example, with image.registry=ghcr.io/owner and tag 0.1.0:

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Value Default Description auth.dev true Built-in development users auth.sessionKey generated Session HMAC key; generated once and preserved auth.sessionTTL 12h Session lifetime auth.secureCookie false Set Secure cookies; enable behind HTTPS auth.existingSecret empty Existing Secret with session-key and oidc-client-secret auth.oidc.issuer empty OIDC issuer; required when auth.dev=false auth.oidc.discoveryURL empty Discovery URL; defaults to the issuer auth.oidc.authorizationURL empty Authorization endpoint override auth.oidc.clientID zeta-portal OIDC client ID auth.oidc.clientSecret empty OIDC client secret auth.oidc.redirectURL auto OIDC callback URL auth.oidc.scopes openid,profile,email,groups OIDC scopes auth.oidc.allowedGroups empty Comma-separated allowed groups auth.oidc.allowedUsers empty Comma-separated allowed usernames, emails, or subjects auth.oidc.usernameClaim preferred_username Username claim auth.oidc.emailClaim email Email claim auth.oidc.groupsClaim groups Groups claim

For production, create the Secret yourself so the client secret is not in the Helm release values:

kubectl -n zeta-poc create secret generic zeta-auth \
  --from-literal=session-key="$(openssl rand -hex 32)" \
  --from-literal=oidc-client-secret='<oidc-secret>'

helm upgrade --install zeta oci://ghcr.io/slimaineb/charts/zeta \
  --version 0.1.0 \
  --namespace zeta-poc \
  --set auth.dev=false \
  --set auth.existingSecret=zeta-auth \
  --set auth.oidc.issuer=https://idp.example.com/realms/dev \
  --set auth.oidc.clientID=zeta-portal \
  --set auth.oidc.redirectURL=https://zeta.example.com/oidc/callback \
  --set auth.secureCookie=true

The Secret must contain the key session-key. oidc-client-secret is optional and is read by the portal through ZETA_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET.

Set auth.oidc.discoveryURL when the portal must fetch discovery from an internal address while auth.oidc.issuer remains the public issuer. Set auth.oidc.authorizationURL when the browser must use a different authorization endpoint than the one in the discovery document.

auth.oidc.allowedGroups and auth.oidc.allowedUsers are optional allowlists. When set, a user must match at least one group and at least one user entry. Entries in allowedUsers can be usernames, emails, or subjects. Claim names can be changed for providers such as Okta or Microsoft Entra ID.

docs.title: Persistence
docs.text:

PVC names are fixed to zeta-poc-artifacts, zeta-poc-cache, and zeta-poc-contexts because the portal uses them directly. They carry helm.sh/resource-policy: keep, so helm uninstall preserves the data.

docs.title: Profiles
docs.text:
Value Default Description profiles.inline empty Inline profiles YAML profiles.existingConfigMap empty Existing ConfigMap with a profiles.yaml key

Profile images use image.registry and image.tag, like the portal and helper images. Use custom profile YAML when a profile needs a different image.

Inline example:

helm upgrade --install zeta ./charts/zeta \
  --namespace zeta-poc \
  --set image.registry=ghcr.io/slimaineb \
  --set image.tag=0.1.0 \
  --set-file profiles.inline=./profiles.yaml

Existing ConfigMap:

kubectl -n zeta-poc create configmap zeta-profiles \
  --from-file=profiles.yaml=./profiles.yaml

helm upgrade --install zeta oci://ghcr.io/slimaineb/charts/zeta \
  --version 0.1.0 \
  --namespace zeta-poc \
  --set profiles.existingConfigMap=zeta-profiles

See Build profiles.

docs.title: Release pipeline
docs.text:
The GitHub Actions workflow .github/workflows/release.yml runs on v* tags:

  1. builds and pushes portal, cpp, go, python-uv, and git-server images to ghcr.io/<owner>/zeta/<image>:<version> and :latest;
  2. builds the CLI for Linux, macOS, and Windows on amd64 and arm64;
  3. packages the chart with the release version as both chart version and appVersion, patches image.registry, and pushes it to oci://ghcr.io/<owner>/charts/zeta;
  4. creates a GitHub Release with the binaries, chart, and checksums.txt.

A v0.1.0 tag therefore produces chart version 0.1.0, image tag 0.1.0, and CLI assets such as zeta-linux-amd64 and zeta-windows-amd64.exe.

docs.title: Install the platform
docs.text: This page installs the Zeta platform with Helm: the portal, RBAC, shared PVCs, and optionally the example Git server. Developers install the CLI separately; see Install the CLI.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Requirement Notes Kubernetes 1.27+ Tested on a single-node k3s cluster. Helm 3.14+ OCI chart support is required. Ingress controller Traefik is the default on k3s; use ingress.className=nginx otherwise. StorageClass local-path works on a single node. Use an EBS/gp3 class for durability and volume expansion. kubectl Access to the target cluster. Docker, k3s, and passwordless sudo Only for the source/local image build.

The published images are public. If the GHCR packages are private, see Private registry.

docs.title: Install the published chart
docs.text:
helm upgrade --install zeta oci://ghcr.io/slimaineb/charts/zeta \
  --version 0.1.0 \
  --namespace zeta-poc --create-namespace \
  --set ingress.host=zeta.local

The chart defaults to:

  • ingress.enabled=true with the traefik class and host zeta.local;
  • development authentication (dev@example.com / dev);
  • local-path storage;
  • no Git server.

Adjust these values for your cluster:

helm upgrade --install zeta oci://ghcr.io/slimaineb/charts/zeta \
  --version 0.1.0 \
  --namespace zeta-poc --create-namespace \
  --set ingress.className=nginx \
  --set ingress.host=zeta.example.com \
  --set portal.storageClass=gp3 \
  --set auth.dev=false \
  --set auth.oidc.issuer=https://idp.example.com/realms/dev \
  --set auth.oidc.clientID=zeta-portal \
  --set auth.oidc.clientSecret='<secret>' \
  --set auth.oidc.redirectURL=https://zeta.example.com/oidc/callback \
  --set auth.oidc.allowedGroups=zeta-users \
  --set auth.secureCookie=true

For a production session key, use a Kubernetes Secret instead of putting it in the command line. Use auth.oidc.allowedUsers or auth.oidc.allowedGroups to restrict sign-in, and adjust the claim names if your provider does not use preferred_username, email, and groups. See Helm chart reference.

docs.title: Private registry
docs.text:
helm registry login authenticates Helm to pull the chart. Kubernetes also needs credentials to pull the images:

echo "$GHCR_TOKEN" | helm registry login ghcr.io -u "$GHCR_USER" --password-stdin

kubectl create namespace zeta-poc --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
kubectl -n zeta-poc create secret docker-registry zeta-pull \
  --docker-server=ghcr.io \
  --docker-username="$GHCR_USER" \
  --docker-password="$GHCR_TOKEN"

helm upgrade --install zeta oci://ghcr.io/slimaineb/charts/zeta \
  --version 0.1.0 \
  --namespace zeta-poc --create-namespace \
  --set image.pullSecrets[0].name=zeta-pull

The chart applies image.pullSecrets to the portal and the optional Git server. Build Jobs use the namespace's default ServiceAccount, so add the same secret there:

kubectl -n zeta-poc patch serviceaccount default -p \
  '{"imagePullSecrets":[{"name":"zeta-pull"}]}'

The scripts/install.sh --registry ghcr.io/<owner> path can create the pull secret automatically when GHCR_TOKEN is set.

docs.title: Install from source
docs.text:
Use this path on a local k3s cluster when you want to build images from the working tree:

./scripts/install.sh

The installer:

  1. checks kubectl and the context (default local);
  2. builds the language, Git server, and portal images;
  3. imports them into k3s containerd;
  4. runs helm upgrade --install with the local chart;
  5. waits for the portal rollout.

Useful options:

./scripts/install.sh --with-git-server
./scripts/install.sh --namespace zeta-dev --context local
./scripts/install.sh --adopt
./scripts/install.sh --dry-run
./scripts/install.sh --help

--adopt migrates an existing raw manifest installation into Helm. It keeps the PVCs and replaces the raw portal Deployment, so expect a short rollout while the new Helm-managed pod starts. Without --adopt, the installer stops if it finds a non-Helm zeta-portal Deployment in the namespace. You can also remove the old installation first:

make uninstall-platform

PVC data

make uninstall-platform deletes the namespace and its PVCs, including caches, artifacts, and environment workspaces. Use --adopt to keep them.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
helm status zeta -n zeta-poc
kubectl -n zeta-poc get deploy,svc,ingress,pods,pvc
curl -fsS http://zeta.local/healthz

curl returns ok. The portal logs should show the listening address and the namespace:

kubectl -n zeta-poc logs deploy/zeta-portal --tail=20

docs.title: Ingress
docs.text:
kubectl -n zeta-poc get ingress zeta-portal

Add the returned address to the hosts file of the machine that opens the browser, and to /etc/hosts in WSL if you use it:

<ADDRESS> zeta.local

docs.title: Port-forward
docs.text:
kubectl -n zeta-poc port-forward --address 0.0.0.0 svc/zeta-portal 8080:80

Open http://localhost:8080. --address 0.0.0.0 is required when the browser runs on Windows and the cluster runs in WSL.

docs.title: Development credentials
docs.text:
Email Password Groups dev@example.com dev devs admin@example.com admin admins alice@example.com alice backend 
zeta login --server http://zeta.local --email dev@example.com --password dev

docs.title: Upgrade
docs.text:
helm upgrade --install zeta oci://ghcr.io/slimaineb/charts/zeta \
  --version 0.2.0 \
  --namespace zeta-poc \
  --reuse-values

--reuse-values keeps your previous overrides. To review the new defaults first:

helm show values oci://ghcr.io/slimaineb/charts/zeta --version 0.2.0

The chart keeps PVCs across upgrades. The portal image tag follows the chart appVersion; helper images (init, syncd, Git server) use the same registry and tag.

docs.title: Uninstall
docs.text:
helm uninstall zeta -n zeta-poc

The shared PVCs have helm.sh/resource-policy: keep, so Helm leaves them in place. To remove everything, including caches, artifacts, and environment workspaces:

kubectl delete namespace zeta-poc

Imported images remain in containerd on a k3s node.

docs.title: HTTP API
docs.text:
All /api/* routes require a session cookie named zeta_session, except the sync agent endpoint which uses a per-environment or per-build bearer token.

Base URL: http://zeta.local (or your ingress/port-forward address).

docs.title: Development login
docs.text:
POST /api/login
Content-Type: application/json

{"username":"dev@example.com","password":"dev"}

Response:

{"email":"dev@example.com","groups":["devs"]}

The response sets the zeta_session cookie.

docs.title: OIDC
docs.text: Route Purpose GET /login Login page / redirect GET /oidc/login?next=/path Start the OIDC flow and return to /path GET /oidc/callback OIDC callback

docs.title: Session
docs.text: Route Purpose GET /api/me Current user POST /api/logout Close the session

docs.title: Sync agent token
docs.text: GET /api/sync/{id}/agent uses Authorization: Bearer <token> instead of the cookie. The token is stored in the Secret zeta-env-<id>-sync (environments) or in the build Job (build sync). ?token=<token> is still accepted for backward compatibility, but new environments and build Jobs use the header.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Errors use a JSON body:

{"error":"profile not found"}
Status Meaning 400 Invalid input, profile, repo, or reference 401 Missing or expired session 403 Cross-origin request or resource owned by another user 404 Build, environment, or volume not found 409 Volume in use or conflicting state 413 Context too large 502 Kubernetes API error

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text:
Method Route Role POST /api/login Development login GET /oidc/login Start OIDC flow GET /oidc/callback OIDC callback POST /api/logout Close session GET /api/me Current user GET /api/profiles Available profiles GET /api/builds List builds POST /api/builds Submit a Git build (JSON) or local-context build (multipart) GET /api/builds/{id}/logs Streaming logs GET /api/builds/{id}/metrics Cache metrics GET /api/builds/{id}/artifact Artifacts as .tar GET /api/sync/{id}/client CLI-side sync WebSocket GET /api/sync/{id}/agent Sidecar sync WebSocket (token) GET /api/volumes Managed PVCs, quota, capacity, last use POST /api/volumes/{name}/resize Expand a managed volume DELETE /api/volumes/{name} Delete an idle managed volume POST /api/envs Create an environment GET /api/envs List environments POST /api/envs/{id}/activate Start an environment POST /api/envs/{id}/deactivate Stop an environment DELETE /api/envs/{id} Delete an environment and its volume GET /api/envs/{id}/exec Interactive exec WebSocket POST /api/envs/{id}/ide Enable the IDE sidecar and return the browser URL GET /api/envs/{id}/ide/ Authenticated HTTP/WebSocket reverse proxy to code-server GET /healthz Health check

Build logs, metrics, and artifacts require the build owner or an admin / admins group member. Environment lifecycle, exec, IDE, and sync endpoints require the environment owner or an admin. Listing builds and environments remains available to all authenticated users.

The IDE proxy accepts the normal portal session cookie. It strips the /api/envs/{id}/ide prefix before forwarding to the code-server sidecar and preserves Upgrade headers for WebSocket traffic. The sidecar itself has authentication disabled and listens only on 127.0.0.1, so it is reachable only through the authenticated portal proxy.

docs.title: Submit a Git build
docs.text:
POST /api/builds
Content-Type: application/json

{"profile":"go","repo":"git://git-server/go.git","commit":"main"}

Response 202 Accepted:

{"id":"zeta-go-8415dfd8487a"}

docs.title: Submit a local-context build
docs.text:
POST /api/builds
Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=...

profile=go
sync=true
context=@context.tar.gz

Fields: profile, repo, commit, sync, and file context (tar.gz).

Constraints:

  • profile must exist.
  • In Git mode, repo must be a git://, http://, https://, or ssh:// URL.
  • commit may be empty, HEAD, a branch, a tag, or a SHA.
  • Upload limited to 512 MiB (2 GiB uncompressed).
  • Absolute paths, .., out-of-context links, and special files are rejected.
  • Shell metacharacters and .. are rejected in Git references.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Zeta separates the control plane from the execution plane. The portal never compiles user code; it creates and observes Kubernetes workloads. Builds and environments run in isolated pods with their own volumes and security context.

flowchart LR
  subgraph workstation["Developer workstation"]
    CLI["zeta CLI"]
  end

  subgraph cluster["Kubernetes cluster (namespace zeta-poc)"]
    Portal["Zeta portal"]
    API["Kubernetes API"]
    Job["Build Job<br/>ephemeral"]
    Env["Environment Deployment<br/>replicas 0 or 1"]
    Cache[("cache PVC")]
    Artifacts[("artifacts PVC")]
    Contexts[("contexts PVC")]
    Workspace[("workspace PVC")]
  end

  CLI -->|"HTTP + session cookie"| Portal
  Portal -->|"ServiceAccount + RBAC"| API
  API -->|"create / watch"| Job
  API -->|"create / scale"| Env
  Job --> Cache
  Job --> Artifacts
  Job --> Contexts
  Env --> Workspace
  Env --> Cache
  Portal -->|"logs, metrics, artifacts"| CLI
  CLI <-->|"WebSocket sync"| Portal
  Portal <-->|"WebSocket sync"| Env

The control plane is small and always available. The execution plane is short-lived: a build exists only for the duration of a Job, and an environment is scaled to zero when idle.

docs.title: Control plane vs execution plane
docs.text: Layer Runs where Responsibility zeta CLI Developer workstation Package the context, call the API, stream logs, receive artifacts, run sync Portal Kubernetes namespace Authenticate users, validate requests, resolve profiles, create Jobs and Deployments, relay logs/artifacts/sync Kubernetes Cluster Schedule and isolate pods, mount PVCs, enforce RBAC and Pod Security Build images Cluster nodes Provide compilers, package managers, Git, and profile-specific toolchains

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
Component Role portal REST API, dev/OIDC auth, embedded web UI, Kubernetes workload creation zeta CLI Login, build submission, logs, status, metrics, artifacts, environments Git server Optional example server with cpp.git, python-uv.git, go.git Build Job Extracts context or clones Git, runs profile commands, writes /artifacts Environment Deployment Long-lived pod with a workspace PVC, a shell, and a sync sidecar Cache PVC Persistent ccache, uv, and Go module/build caches Context PVC Uploaded tar.gz contexts for local-context builds Artifacts PVC Build outputs shared between Jobs and the portal

Kubernetes resources:

  • Namespace: zeta-poc
  • Pod Security Admission: restricted
  • Build Jobs: non-root 1000:1000, no service account token, seccomp RuntimeDefault, all capabilities dropped
  • Portal: non-root 65532:65532, read-only root filesystem
  • Portal RBAC: namespace-scoped access to Jobs, Pods, Pod logs, and PVCs

docs.title: Request flow: build
docs.text:
1. The developer runs zeta build from a project directory.
  2. The CLI detects the profile, builds a filtered tar.gz context, and uploads it to the portal with the session cookie.
  3. The portal validates the archive, stores it on the context PVC, and creates a Job.
  4. The Job init container extracts the context into /workspace (or clones the requested Git commit in Git mode).
  5. The build container runs the profile commands with /cache and /artifacts mounted.
  6. The portal streams logs and status to the CLI and web UI.
  7. When the Job succeeds, the CLI downloads the artifacts as a .tar archive.
  8. The Job and its pod are removed automatically after the configured TTL.
zeta CLI
   |
   |  POST /api/builds (multipart or JSON)
   v
portal ──► create Job ──► init (context/Git) ──► build (profile commands)
   |                                                    |
   |  GET /api/builds/{id}/logs                          ├── /cache (PVC)
   |  GET /api/builds/{id}/metrics                       └── /artifacts (PVC)
   |  GET /api/builds/{id}/artifact
   v
zeta CLI

docs.title: Build Job anatomy
docs.text:
Part Purpose context init container Extracts the uploaded tar.gz or clones the Git commit build container Runs the profile commands in workDir syncd sidecar Only for --sync; relays workspace changes /workspace EmptyDir or context volume used by the build /cache Shared or dedicated cache PVC /artifacts Shared or dedicated artifacts PVC

Security:

  • runAsNonRoot, UID/GID 1000:1000;
  • automountServiceAccountToken: false;
  • seccompProfile: RuntimeDefault;
  • all capabilities dropped;
  • ActiveDeadlineSeconds and TTLSecondsAfterFinished bound the lifetime.

docs.title: Environment anatomy
docs.text:
An environment is a Deployment named zeta-env-<id> with two containers, plus an optional code-server sidecar for the browser IDE:

Deployment zeta-env-<id> (replicas 0 or 1)
  |- env   : profile image, command "sleep infinity", workingDir /workspace
  |          mounts: /workspace (PVC zeta-env-<id>), /cache (shared cache PVC)
  |- syncd : image zeta/portal:0.1, command /syncd
  |          env: ZETA_SYNC_TOKEN (Secret zeta-env-<id>-sync),
  |               ZETA_SYNC_URL=ws://zeta-portal/api/sync/<id>/agent,
  |               ZETA_WORKSPACE=/workspace,
  |               ZETA_SYNC_ENV=1
  |          mounts: /workspace
  `- ide   : image codercom/code-server:<pinned>, listens on 127.0.0.1:8080
             mounts: /workspace, ephemeral /home/coder

The ide container is added when the portal has --ide-image configured. It has no Service or Ingress. The portal authenticates /api/envs/<id>/ide/, opens a port-forward to the pod, and reverse-proxies HTTP and WebSocket traffic to code-server.

The sync Secret is created by zeta init and reused by later activations. If the Secret is missing when the portal needs a session, it recreates it from the Deployment token.

docs.title: Sync hub
docs.text:
The portal keeps an in-memory hub keyed by environment or build ID. Each session holds:

  • the sync token;
  • the CLI and agent WebSocket connections;
  • activity timestamps for clients and exec sessions.

The hub relays messages between the CLI and the syncd sidecar. Activity tracking is also used by the idle reaper.

docs.title: Exec proxy
docs.text:
GET /api/envs/{id}/exec upgrades to a WebSocket and runs a TTY command through the Kubernetes exec API (remotecommand.NewWebSocketExecutor).

Frame format:

First byte Direction Payload i client → server Raw stdin r client → server JSON resize {"cols":80,"rows":24} o server → client Raw stdout/stderr

The shell is non-login and starts in /workspace:

sh -c "cd /workspace && (command -v bash >/dev/null && exec bash -i || exec sh -i)"

docs.title: Idle reaper
docs.text:
RunIdleReaper periodically scans active environments:

  1. tick interval is min(timeout, 1m);
  2. an environment with an attached client or exec is never reaped;
  3. an environment idle for --env-idle-timeout is scaled to zero;
  4. its sync session is deleted and forgotten;
  5. the workspace PVC is preserved.

--env-idle-timeout=0 disables the reaper. The default is 15m.

docs.title: Deletion
docs.text:
DeleteEnvironment deletes the Deployment, pods, sync Secret, and PVC with bounded waits:

  • 45 seconds for pods;
  • 60 seconds for the PVC.

If the PVC is still terminating, the API returns an error explaining that the environment was removed but its volume is still terminating.

docs.title: Data model
docs.text: Type Key fields Build id, profile, language, repo, commit, owner, status, pod, timestamps, durations, cache metrics Profile name, language, image, commands, artifactPath, cacheDir, PVCs, resources, env, metrics Volume name, role, capacity, storageClass, createdAt, last use, inUse, resizable Environment id, profile, owner, active, sizeBytes, storageClass, createdAt EnvSpec / EnvRequest id/name, profile, owner, image, env, size, token

docs.title: Design choices
docs.text:
• Local context first. The default mode works without a Git remote, a webhook, or a pushed commit.
  • Git mode when reproducibility matters. Passing --git or --repo builds an exact commit reachable from the cluster.
  • Profiles instead of hard-coded languages. A profile is an image, commands, resources, environment, and metrics. Adding a language does not change the API.
  • Persistent caches, ephemeral builds. PVCs are mounted only while a pod runs; after the Job is deleted, only storage remains.
  • No user cluster credentials. Authentication and authorization happen at the portal.
  • Observable by default. Logs, durations, cache metrics, and artifacts are exposed through the same API used by the CLI and dashboard.

docs.title: Compute on demand
docs.text:
One of the main goals of Zeta is to avoid keeping a powerful build machine running all the time. You do not need a high-end laptop, a dedicated build server, or a large always-on VM for every developer.

Instead:

  • the control plane is a small portal Deployment that can run on an inexpensive always-on node;
  • build compute is requested only while a build Job is running, then released;
  • CPU and memory limits are set per profile, so heavy C++ or Go builds do not affect other workloads;
  • persistent environments are scaled to zero after --env-idle-timeout (default 15m) and resume from their workspace PVC;
  • caches survive between builds, so paying for compute on demand does not mean rebuilding everything from scratch.

The result is a shared build capacity model: expensive CPU and memory are consumed in bursts, when someone actually needs them, instead of being idle on a developer workstation all day.

docs.title: Failure and recovery
docs.text:
• Portal restart: sync sessions are in memory and are recreated from the Secret when needed. OIDC login flow state is stored in a signed zeta_oidc cookie, so it survives portal restarts and works across replicas. Sessions are invalidated if --oidc-session-key is random.
  • Idle environment: scaled to zero; zeta activate starts it again with the same volume.
  • Stuck build: ActiveDeadlineSeconds terminates it; the TTL removes it.
  • Lost node (local-path): the PVC is node-local; use an EBS-backed StorageClass for durability.

docs.title: Portal configuration
docs.text: The portal is configured with flags or environment variables. Flags take precedence.
