docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• Either --oidc-issuer or --oidc-dev is required.
  • --namespace is required.
  • If --oidc-session-key is empty, a random key is generated at startup. All sessions are invalidated on restart. Set a fixed key in production.

docs.title: OIDC in production
docs.text:
Example Deployment arguments:

args:
  - -addr=:8080
  - -namespace=zeta-poc
  - -oidc-issuer=https://idp.example.com/realms/dev
  - -oidc-discovery-url=https://idp.example.com/realms/dev
  - -oidc-client-id=zeta-portal
  - -oidc-client-secret=<secret>
  - -oidc-redirect-url=https://zeta.example.com/oidc/callback
  - -oidc-allowed-groups=zeta-users
  - -oidc-username-claim=preferred_username
  - -oidc-email-claim=email
  - -oidc-groups-claim=groups
  - -oidc-session-key=<32+ random characters>
  - -oidc-session-ttl=12h
  - -secure-cookie

The OIDC provider must allow exactly the callback URL. The portal uses the configured --oidc-username-claim, --oidc-email-claim, and --oidc-groups-claim; defaults are preferred_username, email, and groups. Groups and profile data are also read from the userinfo endpoint when the ID token does not contain them.

--oidc-allowed-groups and --oidc-allowed-users are optional allowlists. When set, the user must match at least one allowed group and at least one allowed user entry. A user entry can be a username, email, or subject.

Use --oidc-discovery-url when the portal must reach discovery through an internal address while the browser uses a public issuer. Use --oidc-authorization-url when the discovery document advertises an internal authorization endpoint that the browser cannot reach.

The login flow uses PKCE, verifies the ID token nonce, and stores its short-lived state in a signed zeta_oidc cookie, so it works across multiple portal replicas. Sessions are stored in the signed zeta_session cookie. Environments and builds are owner-scoped: lifecycle, exec, sync, logs, metrics, and artifact downloads require the owner or an admin / admins group member. Listing builds and environments remains available to every authenticated user. Full per-group RBAC is still not implemented.

docs.title: Development authentication
docs.text:
With --oidc-dev, the portal accepts the built-in users:

Email Password Groups dev@example.com dev devs admin@example.com admin admins alice@example.com alice backend

docs.title: Environment idle timeout
docs.text:
--env-idle-timeout controls the persistent environment reaper:

  • default 15m;
  • 0 disables automatic scale-down;
  • the portal checks at most once per minute;
  • an environment with an attached shell or sync client is never reaped;
  • scaling down preserves the workspace PVC.

docs.title: Image overrides
docs.text:
--image-registry and --image-tag rewrite the images used by builds:

  • profile images such as zeta/cpp:0.1 become <registry>/zeta/cpp:<tag>;
  • the context init image (zeta/git-server), the sync sidecar (zeta/portal/syncd), and the optional Git server use the same registry and tag;
  • images that already contain a registry (for example ghcr.io/... or localhost/...) are left unchanged;
  • the artifact helper image remains busybox:1.36 from Docker Hub.

Example:

zeta-portal \
  -image-registry=ghcr.io/slimaineb \
  -image-tag=0.1.0

The Helm chart sets these values from image.registry and image.tag. Use the same tag as the portal image so the syncd sidecar matches the portal. See Helm chart reference.

docs.title: Profiles file
docs.text: --profiles-file points to an additional YAML file. It is merged with portal/internal/builds/defaults.yaml by profile name. See Profiles.

docs.title: Storage
docs.text:
• --storage-class is used for shared and environment PVCs unless a profile sets its own storageClass.
  • Storage class is a platform concern and is not configurable from zeta.yaml.
  • --volume-quota and --volume-max are application-level quotas checked on create and expand.

See Volumes and artifacts.

docs.title: Kubernetes resources
docs.text:
The Helm chart in charts/zeta is the recommended installation path. The raw manifests remain for local development and for understanding the resources.

Manifest Contents charts/zeta/ Helm chart for the portal, RBAC, PVCs, Ingress, and optional Git server platform/manifests/namespace.yaml Namespace and Pod Security labels platform/manifests/pvc.yaml Shared artifacts PVC platform/manifests/cache-pvc.yaml Shared build cache PVC platform/manifests/context-pvc.yaml Shared local context PVC platform/manifests/portal.yaml ServiceAccount, RBAC, Deployment, Service, Ingress platform/manifests/git-server.yaml Optional example Git server

docs.title: Naming and labels
docs.text:
Resource Name Namespace zeta-poc Portal Deployment zeta-portal Portal Service zeta-portal Portal Ingress zeta-portal Build Jobs zeta-<profile>-<id> Environment Deployment zeta-env-<id> Environment PVC zeta-env-<id> Environment sync Secret zeta-env-<id>-sync

Managed resources carry zeta.io/managed-by=portal and role/profile labels.

docs.title: Deployment environment
docs.text:
With Helm, configure the portal through values such as portal.storageClass, portal.volumeQuota, portal.envIdleTimeout, auth.*, and image.*; see the Helm chart reference.

The raw platform/manifests/portal.yaml sets the same options in its args list. Adjust it for production and add OIDC values from your secret store.

docs.title: zeta.yaml reference
docs.text: zeta.yaml configures persistent environments. It is read by zeta init, zeta activate, zeta deactivate, and zeta rm. Builds (zeta build) do not read it: they use flags, ZETA_PROFILE, and language auto-detection.

docs.title: Discovery and precedence
docs.text:
• The file is read from the --context directory (default .).
  • context is resolved relative to the directory containing zeta.yaml.
  • CLI flags override file values.
  • The environment name falls back to the context directory name.
  • The StorageClass is a platform setting (--storage-class / ZETA_STORAGE_CLASS), not a project setting.

docs.title: Schema
docs.text:
name: dev
profile: go
image: zeta/go:0.1
context: .
size: 5Gi
exclude:
  - artifacts
  - .cache
env:
  GOFLAGS: -mod=mod
  APP_ENV: development
  PORT: 8080
  DEBUG: true
Field Type Default Description name string directory name Environment name (normalized to a slug) profile string auto-detected Build profile used for the image, cache, and resources image string profile image Base image override for this environment context string . Local directory mirrored into /workspace size string 5Gi Workspace PVC size exclude list of strings [] Extra sync exclusions env mapping {} Extra environment variables

All fields are optional.

docs.title: env values
docs.text:
env accepts any scalar YAML value and stores it as a string, so these are equivalent:

env:
  PORT: 8080
  DEBUG: true
  MODE: development

The environment receives:

PORT=8080
DEBUG=true
MODE=development

Project values override profile values with the same name.

docs.title: Context resolution
docs.text:
If context is relative, it is joined to the directory containing zeta.yaml:

# /home/user/project/zeta.yaml
context: ./src

The mirrored root is /home/user/project/src.

If context is absolute, it is used as-is.

docs.title: Image override
docs.text:
image replaces the profile image for this environment only. The profile still provides the cache PVC, resources, and environment defaults.

profile: go
image: zeta/python-uv:0.1

Useful for a one-off toolchain without creating a new profile.

docs.title: Exclusions
docs.text:
exclude adds to the environment sync exclusions. The defaults already exclude .git, .venv, __pycache__, node_modules, and tool caches. build/ and dist/ are intentionally not excluded so outputs come back locally.

exclude:
  - artifacts
  - tmp
  - "*.log"

docs.title: Name normalization
docs.text:
The name is lowercased. Characters other than a-z, 0-9, and - become -. Leading and trailing dashes are trimmed, and the result is limited to 40 characters. An empty result becomes env.

Examples:

Input Result My Project my-project api_v2 api-v2 -- env

docs.title: Go
docs.text:
name: go-dev
profile: go
size: 5Gi
env:
  GOFLAGS: -mod=mod

docs.title: Python
docs.text:
name: py-dev
profile: python
size: 8Gi
env:
  UV_LINK_MODE: copy

docs.title: C++
docs.text:
name: cpp-dev
profile: cpp
size: 10Gi
exclude:
  - build
  - cmake-build-debug
env:
  CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE: Debug

docs.title: Interaction with commands
docs.text: Command Reads zeta.yaml Uses zeta init yes name, profile, image, size, env zeta activate yes name, context, exclude zeta deactivate yes name, context zeta rm yes name, context zeta build no flags, ZETA_PROFILE, auto-detection

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
• env must be a mapping.
  • size is passed to Kubernetes; invalid values are rejected by the API server or the portal.
  • Unknown fields are ignored by the YAML decoder.

docs.title: Builds
docs.text: A build is an ephemeral Kubernetes Job created by the portal. The source comes either from your local working tree or from a pushed Git commit. The build runs in the profile image with a persistent cache and an artifacts volume.

docs.title: Two modes
docs.text:
Mode Trigger Source Use case Local context zeta build tar.gz of the local directory Experiments, private branches, monorepos Git zeta build --git or --repo Remote commit Reproducible, auditable builds

Local context is the default: no remote, webhook, or pushed commit is required.

docs.title: Profile detection
docs.text:
If --profile is empty, the CLI detects the language:

File present Language Profile CMakeLists.txt cpp cpp go.mod go go pyproject.toml, setup.py, requirements.txt python python

If no profile matches, pass --profile with one of the names returned by zeta profiles.

docs.title: Local context
docs.text:
cd my-project
zeta build

The CLI creates a filtered tar.gz. Default exclusions are:

.git
.venv
build
dist
__pycache__
node_modules
.pytest_cache
.mypy_cache
.ruff_cache
.tox
.cache
.zeta
.zeta-ready

Add exclusions with --exclude (repeatable):

zeta build --exclude .cache --exclude docs

The artifact directory (--artifacts-dir, artifacts by default) is also excluded from the context.

docs.title: Context limits
docs.text:
• Upload limited to 512 MiB.
  • Uncompressed size limited to 2 GiB.
  • Absolute paths, .., out-of-context links, and special files are rejected.
  • There is no .dockerignore: use --exclude and the default exclusions.

docs.title: Git mode
docs.text:
zeta build --git --profile cpp \
  --repo git://git-server/cpp.git \
  --commit main
  • --repo enables Git mode; --git alone uses the current repository remote.
  • --commit accepts a branch, tag, HEAD, or SHA. Empty uses the current branch.
  • Accepted URL schemes are git://, http://, https://, and ssh://.
  • file:// URLs and local paths are rejected.
  • Shell metacharacters and .. are rejected in Git references.
  • A local unpushed commit is not visible from the cluster.

With the example Git server, the in-cluster URL is git://git-server/<repo>.git. To clone locally, use a port-forward:

kubectl --context local -n zeta-poc port-forward svc/git-server 19418:9418
git clone git://127.0.0.1:19418/cpp.git

The 127.0.0.1:19418 URL is not reachable from the cluster: for builds, use git://git-server/cpp.git.

docs.title: Sync during a build
docs.text:
zeta build --sync

Sync mode adds a syncd sidecar and a WebSocket relay:

zeta CLI <--- WebSocket ---> portal sync hub <--- WebSocket ---> syncd
                                                                   |
                                                             /workspace
                                                             /artifacts

Flow:

  1. The initial context is synchronized before the build starts.
  2. The build waits for the /workspace/.zeta-ready marker.
  3. Local edits are sent to the pod while the build runs.
  4. Files created in /workspace and artifacts are sent back.
  5. A final flush writes the latest artifacts to artifacts/<id>.

Default exclusions prevent local outputs (build, dist, .venv, etc.) from being overwritten. --sync is incompatible with Git.

The build timeout is also the sync timeout (--timeout, 30m by default).

docs.title: Follow a build
docs.text:
zeta builds
zeta status zeta-go-xxxxxxxxxxxx
zeta logs zeta-go-xxxxxxxxxxxx
zeta metrics zeta-go-xxxxxxxxxxxx
zeta artifacts -o artifacts.tar zeta-go-xxxxxxxxxxxx

Possible statuses:

Status Meaning pending Job created, pod not started yet running Build in progress succeeded Build succeeded failed Build failed unknown State could not be determined

docs.title: Artifacts
docs.text:
The exported directory is the profile's artifactPath:

Profile Directory cpp /artifacts/cpp python /artifacts/python go /artifacts/go

zeta build downloads and extracts artifacts by default. To fetch them later:

zeta artifacts -o build.tar zeta-go-xxxxxxxxxxxx

The archive contains the contents of artifactPath. Artifacts are stored per language, not per build: a newer build of the same profile can overwrite the previous artifact directory on the shared PVC.

docs.title: Artifact exclusions
docs.text:
Configure artifactExclude in the profile, or use the flag:

zeta build --artifact-exclude '*.log' --artifact-exclude 'coverage/'

Patterns are passed to tar --exclude on the portal, applied during local extraction, and ignored by the sync client.

docs.title: Concurrency
docs.text:
Each profile defaults to maxConcurrent: 1. Builds of the same profile are serialized because they write to the same artifactPath. Different profiles can run in parallel.

Increase maxConcurrent only when each build writes to a unique artifactPath; otherwise artifacts can overwrite each other.

docs.title: Lifetime
docs.text:
• Jobs have a 1 hour TTL (TTLSecondsAfterFinished: 3600).
  • ActiveDeadlineSeconds is 3600 for a normal build and 1800 for a sync build.
  • A stuck build therefore cannot run forever.
  • Jobs and their logs disappear from the cluster and UI after the TTL.

Manual deletion:

kubectl --context local -n zeta-poc delete job \
  -l zeta.io/managed-by=portal

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
• Use --sync to debug without rebuilding the environment manually.
  • Use Git mode for reproducible, shareable builds.
  • Keep caches on PVCs; do not put them in the local context.
  • Add --exclude for large generated directories.
  • Check zeta volumes before deleting a cache.

docs.title: zeta CLI
docs.text: The CLI is the developer entry point. It packages the context, calls the portal API, streams logs, downloads artifacts, and manages persistent environments.

docs.title: Local configuration
docs.text:
The session is stored in ~/.config/zeta/config.json with mode 0600. zeta logout only removes the local session.

Variable Purpose ZETA_SERVER Portal URL, for example http://zeta.local ZETA_COOKIE Session cookie (raw value or full cookie) ZETA_PROFILE Default profile for zeta build

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Command Purpose zeta login Log in (dev mode or OIDC cookie) zeta logout Remove the local session zeta profiles List available profiles zeta build Run a local or Git build zeta builds List builds zeta status ID Show build details zeta logs ID Stream build logs zeta metrics ID Show cache metrics zeta artifacts ID Download build artifacts zeta volumes List managed volumes zeta volumes resize NAME SIZE Expand a volume zeta volumes delete NAME Delete an idle volume zeta init Provision a persistent environment zeta activate Start it, open a shell, and sync files zeta deactivate Scale it to zero zeta ls List environments zeta rm Delete an environment and its volume

The aliases zeta up / zeta down map to activate / deactivate. zeta env <init|activate|deactivate|ls|rm> is still accepted for compatibility.

docs.title: Development mode
docs.text:
zeta login \
  --server http://zeta.local \
  --email dev@example.com \
  --password dev
Flag Description --server Portal URL (or ZETA_SERVER) --email Email (dev mode) --password Password (dev mode) --cookie Existing session cookie (OIDC mode)

If --email or --password is omitted, the CLI prompts for it.

docs.title: OIDC mode
docs.text:
Browser integration is not available in the CLI yet. Copy the zeta_session cookie from the browser, then:

zeta login --server https://zeta.example.com --cookie '<cookie_value>'

docs.title: Profiles
docs.text:
zeta profiles

Shows the name, language, default repository, and description of each profile. See Profiles.

docs.title: Local build (default)
docs.text:
cd my-project
zeta build

The CLI:

  1. detects the profile from CMakeLists.txt, go.mod, or pyproject.toml / setup.py / requirements.txt;
  2. creates a filtered tar.gz of the current directory;
  3. uploads it to the portal with the session cookie;
  4. streams logs live;
  5. waits for the build to finish;
  6. downloads and extracts artifacts into artifacts/<id>.

docs.title: zeta build flags
docs.text:
Flag Default Description --profile NAME auto Force the profile --context DIR . Local directory to upload --exclude PATTERN — Context exclusion (repeatable) --artifact-exclude PATTERN — Downloaded artifact exclusion (repeatable) --git false Enable Git mode --repo URL — Repository URL (enables Git mode) --commit REF current branch Branch, tag, or SHA --follow true Follow logs live --artifacts true Download and extract artifacts --artifacts-dir DIR artifacts Artifact output directory --sync false Bidirectional sync during the build --timeout DURATION 30m Build wait timeout

Constraints:

  • --context and --git / --repo are incompatible.
  • --commit requires --git or --repo.
  • --sync is incompatible with Git mode.

docs.title: Git build
docs.text:
zeta build --git --profile go \
  --repo git://git-server/go.git \
  --commit main

The commit must already be pushed and reachable from the cluster. A local unpushed commit cannot be cloned by the Job.

docs.title: Typical output
docs.text:
context: /home/user/my-project (27 KB)
build zeta-go-xxxxxxxxxxxx (go) context /home/user/my-project
--- logs ---
[ live build logs ]
build succeeded in 12.4 s
cache: 12 hits / 3 miss (80%) · 84 MB
artifacts: /home/user/my-project/artifacts/zeta-go-xxxxxxxxxxxx

docs.title: Interactive sync
docs.text:
zeta build --sync

The build waits for /workspace/.zeta-ready, syncs the initial context, then exchanges local changes and pod-side files. A final flush collects the latest artifacts before exit.

docs.title: Inspect builds
docs.text:
zeta builds
zeta status zeta-go-xxxxxxxxxxxx
zeta logs zeta-go-xxxxxxxxxxxx
zeta metrics zeta-go-xxxxxxxxxxxx
zeta artifacts -o artifacts.tar zeta-go-xxxxxxxxxxxx

zeta metrics returns JSON:

{
  "hits": 5,
  "misses": 1,
  "hitRate": 83.33,
  "sizeBytes": 43628
}

Flag order

Flags must come before the build ID: zeta artifacts -o out.tar ID, zeta status --json ID.

docs.title: Volumes
docs.text:
zeta volumes
zeta volumes --role cache
zeta volumes --older-than 720h
zeta volumes --json
zeta volumes resize zeta-poc-cache 5Gi
zeta volumes delete zeta-test-cache

--older-than is a reporting filter: Zeta does not delete volumes automatically. A volume in use by a build cannot be resized or deleted.

See Volumes and artifacts.

docs.title: Persistent environments
docs.text:
zeta init
zeta activate
zeta ls
zeta deactivate
zeta rm
Command Flags zeta init --name, --profile, --context, --size zeta activate --name, --context, --exclude (repeatable) zeta code --name, --context, --print zeta deactivate --name, --context zeta ls --json zeta rm [NAME], --name, --context

The name is resolved in this order: --name flag, name field in zeta.yaml, then the context directory name. It is normalized to a slug (lowercase letters, digits, and dashes, up to 40 characters).

zeta init, activate, code, deactivate, and rm read zeta.yaml from --context (default .). Flags take precedence over the file.

zeta code starts the environment, enables the code-server sidecar if the environment predates it, and opens the authenticated browser IDE on /workspace. Use --print on headless machines and open the printed URL manually.

See Persistent environments and zeta.yaml reference.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
Code Meaning 0 Success 1 CLI error, failed build, missing session, or rejected request

Errors are written to stderr with the zeta: prefix.

docs.title: Help
docs.text:
zeta help
zeta --help

docs.title: Persistent environments
docs.text: A build is disposable. An environment is a long-lived pod backed by a persistent volume and kept in sync with your local directory. It stays available between commands, so you can run go build, make, tests, or a debugger without waiting for a new pod each time.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
zeta init        # create the volume, sync secret, and stopped deployment
zeta activate    # start the pod, open a shell in /workspace, mirror files
zeta ls          # list environments
zeta deactivate  # scale the pod to zero, keep the volume
zeta rm          # delete everything, including the volume
Command Effect zeta init Creates PVC zeta-env-<id>, Secret zeta-env-<id>-sync, and Deployment zeta-env-<id> at 0 replicas zeta activate Scales to 1, starts the sync client, and opens an interactive shell zeta code Starts the pod if needed and opens VS Code in the browser on /workspace zeta deactivate Scales to 0 and drops the sync session zeta rm Deletes the Deployment, pods, Secret, and PVC

zeta up / zeta down are aliases for activate / deactivate.

docs.title: Naming
docs.text:
The environment name is resolved from:

  1. --name;
  2. the name field in zeta.yaml;
  3. the context directory name.

It is normalized to a slug: lowercase letters, digits, and dashes, up to 40 characters.

docs.title: zeta.yaml
docs.text:
Most options live in zeta.yaml at the project root:

name: dev
profile: go
image: zeta/go:0.1        # optional base image override
context: .                # directory mirrored into /workspace
size: 5Gi
exclude:
  - artifacts
env:
  GOFLAGS: -mod=mod
  APP_ENV: development

zeta.yaml is read from the --context directory (default .), and context is resolved relative to it. CLI flags override the file.

See zeta.yaml reference.

docs.title: What gets mirrored
docs.text:
The environment uses a different exclusion set from builds: dependencies and caches stay remote, but build outputs are synced back.

Excluded from the mirror:

.git
.venv
__pycache__
node_modules
.pytest_cache
.mypy_cache
.ruff_cache
.tox
.cache
.zeta
.zeta-ready

build/ and dist/ are not excluded, so outputs produced inside the pod come back to your machine. Add extra exclusions with --exclude (repeatable) or the exclude list in zeta.yaml.

docs.title: The shell
docs.text:
zeta activate starts the pod, waits for the initial sync, and opens a shell in /workspace. The shell is interactive and non-login:

sh -c "cd /workspace && (command -v bash >/dev/null && exec bash -i || exec sh -i)"

Leaving the shell (Ctrl-D or exit) does not stop the environment. Run zeta deactivate explicitly when you are done, or let the idle reaper stop it.

docs.title: VS Code in the browser
docs.text:
zeta code opens a browser IDE backed by the environment workspace:

zeta code
zeta code --print        # print the URL without launching a browser

The portal authenticates the request, then reverse-proxies HTTP and WebSocket traffic to a code-server sidecar in the environment pod. The sidecar listens on 127.0.0.1:8080 and is never exposed by a Service or Ingress; the portal reaches it through the Kubernetes port-forward API. The browser URL is:

http://<portal>/api/envs/<id>/ide/

The sidecar shares /workspace with the env container, so edits, builds, and terminals opened in VS Code see the same files as zeta activate. The IDE session is tied to the pod lifetime and is counted as activity by the idle reaper. zeta code adds the sidecar to an existing environment on first use; allow a short rollout while the new pod starts.

docs.title: Idle scale-down
docs.text:
To save compute, the portal scales an environment back to zero when no shell or sync client has been attached for --env-idle-timeout:

  • default: 15m;
  • 0 disables the reaper;
  • the reaper checks at most once per minute;
  • the volume and its contents are preserved;
  • the next zeta activate resumes quickly.

The portal logs a line such as:

env reaper: dev scaled to zero after 15m0s idle

docs.title: Storage
docs.text:
Item Default Workspace PVC zeta-env-<id>, 5Gi StorageClass platform --storage-class (default local-path) Cache shared profile cache PVC (default zeta-poc-cache, 2Gi)

The workspace PVC is mounted at /workspace; the cache is mounted at /cache. The volume is labeled zeta.io/volume-role=env and kept across deactivate/activate.

docs.title: Image and environment overrides
docs.text:
image overrides the profile base image for this environment. env is merged with the profile environment; project values win by name.

Example: profile go with a Python image for a one-off environment:

name: py-playground
profile: go
image: zeta/python-uv:0.1
env:
  CUSTOM: "yes"

The deployment uses zeta/python-uv:0.1 and keeps the profile's cache and resource settings.

docs.title: Deletion and timeouts
docs.text:
zeta rm deletes the Deployment, its pods, the sync Secret, and the PVC. The portal waits up to 45 seconds for pods and 60 seconds for the PVC. If the volume is still terminating, the request fails with:

environment <id> was removed but its volume is still terminating

Retry after the volume finalizer completes.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Environments share the zeta-poc namespace and the portal RBAC. Environments are owner-scoped for lifecycle, exec, and sync operations; admin / admins group members can manage any environment. There is no full per-group isolation yet.
  • Sync is last-writer-wins; simultaneous edits on both sides can conflict.
  • local-path volumes are node-local. Use an EBS-backed StorageClass in production.
  • The workspace is mirrored, not mounted over the network. Large trees take longer to sync initially.
  • The sync sidecar uses zeta/portal:0.1; keep that image available in containerd.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom Check activate hangs kubectl -n zeta-poc get pods, kubectl -n zeta-poc logs deploy/zeta-env-<id> -c syncd Shell exits immediately Check the env container logs; the image must have a shell Files do not come back Check exclude and the build/, dist/ paths Environment stops by itself Idle timeout; run zeta activate again rm returns 504 The portal restarted or the PVC is terminating; retry Pod stays Pending Check the PVC and StorageClass

See Troubleshooting for more.

docs.title: Build profiles
docs.text:
A profile describes how to build one language: the image, the commands, the artifact path, the cache, the resources, the environment, and the metrics.

Profiles are loaded from portal/internal/builds/defaults.yaml and merged with the optional --profiles-file / ZETA_PROFILES_FILE file. Merging is by name: a custom profile can replace cpp, python, or go, or add a new one.

docs.title: Built-in profiles
docs.text:
Profile Language Image Artifacts Cache cpp C++ zeta/cpp:0.1 /artifacts/cpp /cache/ccache python Python 3.12 + uv zeta/python-uv:0.1 /artifacts/python /cache/uv go Go zeta/go:0.1 /artifacts/go /cache/go-build, /cache/go-mod

The Go profile:

  • sets PATH so /usr/local/go/bin is available in the build container;
  • sets GOCACHE and GOMODCACHE;
  • runs go mod download, go test ./..., and either go build ./cmd/... or go build . depending on the project layout;
  • reports cache_bytes.

docs.title: Registry and tag overrides
docs.text:
Profiles in the defaults use short image names such as zeta/cpp:0.1. The portal can rewrite them at startup:

zeta-portal -image-registry=ghcr.io/slimaineb -image-tag=0.1.0

or with environment variables:

ZETA_IMAGE_REGISTRY=ghcr.io/slimaineb ZETA_IMAGE_TAG=0.1.0 zeta-portal

The override applies to every profile image and to the helper images used by builds (context init, syncd, and the optional Git server). Images that already include a registry are left unchanged. The Helm chart wires this automatically from image.registry / image.tag.

See Portal configuration.

docs.title: Schema
docs.text:
profiles:
  - name: cpp
    description: C++ CMake/Ninja with persistent ccache
    language: cpp
    image: zeta/cpp:0.1
    defaultRepo: git://git-server/cpp.git
    workDir: /workspace
    artifactPath: /artifacts/cpp
    cacheDir: /cache/ccache
    # Optional: use a dedicated cache PVC instead of the shared one
    cachePVC: zeta-cpp-cache
    cacheSize: 5Gi
    # Optional: use a dedicated artifacts PVC instead of the shared one
    artifactsPVC: zeta-cpp-artifacts
    artifactsSize: 2Gi
    # Optional: StorageClass for dedicated volumes (default: portal setting)
    storageClass: ebs-sc
    # Optional: files never copied back from the build pod
    artifactExclude:
      - "*.o"
      - "*.d"
    # Optional: concurrent builds for this profile (default: 1)
    maxConcurrent: 1
    envFromSecrets:
      - zeta-build-secrets
    resources:
      cpuRequest: 200m
      memoryRequest: 256Mi
      cpuLimit: "2"
      memoryLimit: 2Gi
      ephemeralStorage: 2Gi
    commands:
      - |
        export CCACHE_DIR=/cache/ccache
        export CCACHE_MAXSIZE=2G
        export CCACHE_BASEDIR=/workspace
        cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
          -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER_LAUNCHER=ccache \
          -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_LAUNCHER=ccache
        cmake --build build
        cmake --install build --prefix /artifacts/cpp
    metrics:
      - name: ccache_hits
        command: ccache -s | awk '/Hits:/ {print $2}'
      - name: ccache_misses
        command: ccache -s | awk '/Misses:/ {print $2}'
      - name: cache_bytes
        command: du -sb /cache/ccache | cut -f1

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Required Description name yes Profile identifier language yes Displayed language image yes Build image commands yes Shell commands executed in workDir artifactPath yes Directory exported as a .tar description no Display text defaultRepo no Default repository workDir no Defaults to /workspace cacheDir no Informational cache path cachePVC no Dedicated cache PVC; defaults to the shared cache PVC cacheSize no Size used when creating cachePVC; defaults to 2Gi artifactsPVC no Dedicated artifacts PVC; defaults to the shared artifacts PVC artifactsSize no Size used when creating artifactsPVC; defaults to 1Gi storageClass no StorageClass for dedicated PVCs; defaults to the portal --storage-class artifactExclude no Glob patterns excluded from artifact download and sync maxConcurrent no Maximum concurrent builds for this profile; defaults to 1 env no Literal environment variables injected into context and build envFromSecrets no Optional Secrets injected with envFrom resources no CPU, memory, and ephemeral-storage requests/limits metrics no Metric commands run after the build

docs.title: Environment variables and Secrets
docs.text:
env injects literal variables. envFromSecrets references Kubernetes Secrets. Secret references are marked optional: true, so a build still runs when the Secret does not exist.

To provide repository or private-module credentials, create the zeta-build-secrets Secret in the namespace:

kubectl --context local -n zeta-poc create secret generic zeta-build-secrets \
  --from-literal=GIT_TOKEN=ghp_xxx \
  --from-literal=GIT_USERNAME=x-access-token \
  --from-literal=GOPRIVATE=github.com/my-org/* \
  --from-literal=GOPROXY=https://proxy.golang.org,direct

The cpp, python, and go profiles already reference it. If GIT_TOKEN is present, the portal configures a Git HTTPS credential helper in the init container and in the build container when git is available.

Supported variables include:

  • GIT_TOKEN
  • GIT_USERNAME
  • GOPRIVATE
  • GOPROXY
  • GONOSUMDB
  • GONOPROXY

Private SSH repositories are not supported.

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
After the build commands, the portal runs the metrics commands with set +e. Each line in this format is parsed:

ZETA_METRIC name=value

Known metrics:

  • ccache_hits
  • ccache_misses
  • cache_bytes

Other metrics are kept in extra and displayed as chips.

docs.title: Custom profiles in Kubernetes
docs.text:
Create a ConfigMap:

kubectl --context local -n zeta-poc create configmap zeta-profiles \
  --from-file=profiles.yaml=./profiles.yaml

Add a volume and the -profiles-file=/etc/zeta/profiles.yaml argument to the Deployment:

kubectl --context local -n zeta-poc patch deploy zeta-portal --type=json -p='[
  {"op":"add","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/args/-","value":"-profiles-file=/etc/zeta/profiles.yaml"},
  {"op":"add","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/volumeMounts","value":[{"name":"profiles","mountPath":"/etc/zeta","readOnly":true}]},
  {"op":"add","path":"/spec/template/spec/volumes","value":[{"name":"profiles","configMap":{"name":"zeta-profiles"}}]}
]'
kubectl --context local -n zeta-poc rollout status deploy/zeta-portal

If the Deployment already has volumes, adapt the patch instead of replacing the arrays.

docs.title: Adding a new profile
docs.text:
1. Build a container image with the toolchain.
  2. Import it into k3s (docker save ... | sudo -n k3s ctr images import -).
  3. Add a profile entry to portal/internal/builds/defaults.yaml or a custom profiles file.
  4. Redeploy the portal if you changed defaults.yaml.
  5. Verify with zeta profiles and a small build.

docs.title: Concurrency and artifacts
docs.text:
Each profile defaults to maxConcurrent: 1. Builds of the same profile are serialized because they write to the same artifactPath. Different profiles can run in parallel.

Set maxConcurrent above 1 only when each build writes to a unique artifactPath; otherwise concurrent builds can overwrite each other's artifacts.

To keep large or sensitive files out of downloads, configure artifactExclude:

artifactExclude:
  - "*.log"
  - "coverage/"
  - "**/*.tmp"

The portal passes these patterns to tar --exclude before streaming artifacts. The CLI also applies them while extracting locally, and the sync client ignores them when receiving artifacts. Use zeta build --artifact-exclude PATTERN for a one-off exclusion; the flag can be repeated.

docs.title: Volume strategy
docs.text:
By default all profiles share these PVCs:

Role Default PVC Mount Contents cache zeta-poc-cache /cache Compiler, package, and module caches artifacts zeta-poc-artifacts /artifacts Build outputs context zeta-poc-contexts /contexts Uploaded local contexts

Set cachePVC / artifactsPVC to give a profile dedicated volumes. A dedicated volume is created on first use with the requested size and storageClass, then reused. Existing PVCs are never resized or recreated automatically.

See Volumes and artifacts.

docs.title: Volumes and artifacts
docs.text: Zeta separates three storage roles. PVCs are mounted only while a build pod or an environment pod is running; after the workload stops, only the storage remains. This is the same cost model as an EBS volume attached during a build and detached afterwards.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text:
Role Default PVC Mount Contents cache zeta-poc-cache /cache Compiler, package, and module caches artifacts zeta-poc-artifacts /artifacts Build outputs context zeta-poc-contexts /contexts Uploaded local contexts env zeta-env-<id> /workspace Persistent environment workspace

By default all profiles share the cache, artifacts, and context PVCs. Set cachePVC / artifactsPVC in a profile to give it dedicated volumes instead. A dedicated volume is created on first use with the requested size and storageClass, then reused on later builds. Existing PVCs are never resized or recreated automatically.

docs.title: Labels and annotations
docs.text:
The portal labels managed PVCs with:

  • zeta.io/managed-by=portal
  • zeta.io/volume-role

It records last use in annotations:

  • zeta.io/last-used-at
  • zeta.io/last-build
  • zeta.io/last-profile
  • zeta.io/last-owner

Environment PVCs are additionally labeled with zeta.io/env=<id>.

docs.title: List volumes
docs.text:
zeta volumes

NAME                 ROLE       SIZE    LAST USE                       BUILD
zeta-poc-artifacts   artifacts  1.0 GB  2026-11-08 18:59 (just now)   zeta-go-8415dfd8487a
zeta-poc-cache       cache      2.0 GB  2026-11-08 18:59 (just now)   zeta-go-8415dfd8487a
zeta-poc-contexts    context    2.0 GB  2026-11-08 18:59 (just now)   zeta-go-8415dfd8487a

Filters:

zeta volumes --role cache
zeta volumes --older-than 720h
zeta volumes --json

--older-than keeps volumes whose last build is older than the given duration. It is a reporting filter: Zeta does not delete volumes automatically.

The quota is displayed above the volume table:

quota: 5.0 GiB / 20 GiB used, 15 GiB free (max per volume: 10 GiB)

docs.title: Resize or delete
docs.text:
zeta volumes resize zeta-poc-cache 5Gi
zeta volumes delete zeta-test-cache

The same actions are available from the Volumes panel in the web UI.

Rules:

  • A volume cannot be resized or deleted while a build is using it.
  • Expansion requires a StorageClass with allowVolumeExpansion: true.
  • The k3s local-path class does not support expansion; use an EBS-backed class in production.
  • Quotas are checked on create and expand.

docs.title: Quotas
docs.text:
The portal enforces two application-level quotas:

  • --volume-quota / ZETA_VOLUME_QUOTA (default 20Gi): total capacity of all managed volumes.
  • --volume-max / ZETA_VOLUME_MAX (default 10Gi): maximum size of one volume.

These are not Kubernetes ResourceQuota objects; the portal checks them itself so it can return a clear error.

docs.title: Reset the cache
docs.text:
Shared cache

Deleting the cache PVC removes ccache, uv, and Go caches for all builds that use it.

zeta volumes --role cache
kubectl --context local -n zeta-poc delete job \
  -l zeta.io/managed-by=portal --ignore-not-found
kubectl --context local -n zeta-poc delete pvc zeta-poc-cache

The PVC is recreated on the next build. Profiles with a dedicated cachePVC keep their own volume.

docs.title: Reset artifacts
docs.text:
zeta volumes --role artifacts
kubectl --context local -n zeta-poc delete pvc zeta-poc-artifacts

The shared PVC is recreated on the next build. Profiles with a dedicated artifactsPVC keep their own volume.

docs.title: Production storage
docs.text: On k3s the default StorageClass is local-path, so volumes are node-local. In production, set the portal --storage-class / ZETA_STORAGE_CLASS to an EBS-backed StorageClass, or set storageClass per profile for dedicated volumes. This gives the expected durability and attach/detach behavior.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Artifacts are stored per language path, not per build. A newer build of the same profile can overwrite the previous artifact directory.
  • There is no automatic volume garbage collection.
  • Deleting a namespace deletes all its PVCs.
  • zeta volumes delete is a convenience wrapper; you can also use kubectl.
